Subject: Structured output acceptance criteria & fallback plan

Hi Samir — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and recommended next steps from our side so we have shared acceptance criteria for the structured-output portion of the proof-of-concept (PoC).

High-level acceptance criteria (proposed):
- JSON schema compliance: 98% of responses must validate against the agreed schema for the first three tokens of the structured block.
- Semantic correctness: key fields (patient_id, diagnosis_code, recommended_action) must match ground truth > 92% on the provided test set.
- Latency: 95th percentile for a 512-token prompt < 350ms on Dedicated tier.
- Graceful degradation: if schema validation fails, the system should return a structured fallback with error_code and raw_text for manual triage.

Recommended model / config for initial PoC:
- Model: rw-infer-large-v1 (8-bit) for highest fidelity on structured extraction.
- Fallback: rw-fast-7b-int4 with stricter output filters for latency-sensitive flows.
- Runtime: enable prefix KV caching and continuous batching; suggested batch-window 20ms for interactive demo.

Validation plan and tooling:
- We'll provide a JSON schema file and an AJV validation harness.
- Suggest 3 retry attempts on transient generation errors with exponential backoff (200ms -> 600ms -> 1800ms) before returning fallback.
- We'll share a small benchmark CSV and the prompt/test-set we used.

Next steps I propose:
1) Share the schema and the test prompts (we attached schema-acceptance-checklist.md and medisoft-benchmarks-20261212.csv).
2) Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive next week (Aditya and Marissa to join) to run a live validation and tune retry policy.
3) If the PoC metrics look good, procurement can start contract paperwork (we can share a PO template).

Attachments: medisoft-benchmarks-20261212.csv, schema-acceptance-checklist.md, PO template (see attachment list).

Thanks — Monica

Couple of technical notes we should surface in the deep-dive and a short roadmap for the PoC run. Copying Marissa for benchmarking context.

Technical notes / recommendations:
- Validation placement: run AJV as a synchronous post-generation check in the serving layer. Stream the token output to the client while validating; if validation fails, send a structured fallback event (error_code: SCHEMA_MISMATCH) and trigger retry logic server-side. This keeps UX snappy while preserving audit logs.
- Retry policy: implement 3 server-side retries with token-diff-based deduplication to avoid repeated identical generations. If retries fail, return fallback JSON containing {error_code, raw_text_snippet, model_version}.
- Cost estimate: empirical results from similar PoCs show retries add ~1.8x token consumption in the worst case. For planning, assume 2x token usage for conservative budget planning; we'll provide a more precise number after the benchmark run.
- Model suggestions: primary rw-infer-large-v1 (8-bit) for accuracy; secondary rw-fast-7b-int4 as cheap/fast fallback. For throughput tests we can also try rw-slim-3b-int4 (very low cost) to characterize degradation curves.

Benchmarking plan:
- We'll run three profiles: accuracy (100 labeled prompts), latency (1000 interactive prompts at concurrency 8), and resilience (schema perturbations + malformed prompts). Results will be uploaded to the Drive folder (link below).

Security/compliance notes:
- Logs: by default, inference logs redact PII/PHI. For Medisoft we can enable encrypted logging with a customer-managed KMS and a retention policy you set. We will not surface raw PHI in the fallback unless you explicitly opt-in for diagnostic export; otherwise raw_text_snippet will be hashed.

Operational asks for Medisoft team before PoC start:
1) Final schema file and representative test prompts (you can upload to the Drive folder).
2) Contact for SSO/KMS setup (procurement or infra).
3) PO timeline so we can reserve Dedicated slots.

I'll prepare a short runbook (checklist + Jenkins-like job definitions) and drop it into the Drive.

-Aditya
